source_case: A target merge can commit while compatibility publication fails, leaving the source prepared. Target reset/erase/retention removes its receipt and rotates grant authority. Retrying the source sends receiptRequired=false, so current handleTransfer remerges captured behavior and issues a new grant in the rotated epoch. This is source-confirmed, not a runtime reproduction.
resolved_preflight_comments: Clarified that a cold or validated pre-authority target may initialize empty authority exactly once; blanket rejection of missing authority would prevent first links. Prior transition/barrier markers prohibit initialization.
Corrected baseline wording from independently reproduced to independently source-confirmed; no runtime probe is claimed.
implementation_review_conditions: Epoch admission is internal-only, bound to the exact recognized target, and serialized. It validates target identity, paired profile state and prior-key safety before any one-time initialization; malformed existing authority is never replaced.

Only an unprepared source requests the target epoch. Persist it in the immutable descriptor and fingerprint; old or malformed prepared records refuse without reacquisition, mutation or renewal. Preserve source grant/expiry checks around awaited work.

Target compares the immutable epoch to current durable authority inside serialization before profile merge, receipt/grant/member writes or compatibility publication. Missing authority at transfer admission is failure, not another cold initialization.

The target admission operation makes no callback to the source. Source-to-recognized-target ordering therefore introduces no serialization cycle; recognized subjects are already prohibited as link sources.

Rejected or commit-ambiguous authority initialization must recover by rereading durable state. Successful acquisition must preserve profile, consent, existing grants and timers. A fresh source after a barrier may use its current epoch; an older prepared source cannot.
